what_its_for: Bexarotene is used to treat a type of skin cancer called cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL). It belongs to a group of medicines called retinoids, which are related to vitamin A. It helps slow down or stop the growth of cancer cells in your skin.
how_to_take: Take bexarotene capsules by mouth with a meal. Swallow the capsules whole — do not crush, chew, or open them. Taking it with food helps your body absorb the medicine better and may reduce stomach upset. Try to take it at the same time each day.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your body size (height and weight). The usual starting dose is 300 mg per square meter of body surface area, taken once daily with a meal. Your doctor may adjust your dose depending on how you respond to the medicine and any side effects you experience. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose as scheduled. Do not take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store bexarotene capsules at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the capsules away from light, heat, and moisture. Do not store them in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use capsules past the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking vitamin A supplements or any other products containing high amounts of vitamin A while on this medicine, as this can increase the risk of serious side effects. Limit your intake of grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as they can affect how your body processes the medicine. Avoid prolonged exposure to sunlight and tanning beds, since bexarotene can make your skin more sensitive to the sun. Use sunscreen and protective clothing when going outdoors. Do not get pregnant while taking this medicine — it can cause serious birth defects. Women of childbearing age must use two reliable forms of birth control during treatment and for at least one month after stopping the medicine. Men should also use a condom during this time. Do not donate blood while taking this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: signs of high triglycerides or cholesterol (which may have no symptoms, so regular blood tests are important), unusual weight gain or swelling, feeling very cold or tired, slow heartbeat, dry or yellowing skin, signs of infection such as fever or chills, severe stomach pain, vision changes, confusion, or if you become pregnant or think you might be pregnant. Also call your doctor if you develop severe skin reactions, muscle weakness, or unusual bleeding.
when_it_works: Bexarotene does not work overnight. Some patients may begin to see improvement in their skin symptoms within a few weeks, but it often takes several months to see the full benefit of treatment. Keep taking the medicine as directed even if you do not notice immediate changes. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular check-ups and blood tests.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine must NOT be used during pregnancy because it can cause severe birth defects. Women who could become pregnant must have a negative pregnancy test before starting treatment and every month during treatment. Two forms of birth control must be used. Breastfeeding is not recommended while taking this medicine. Children: The safety and effectiveness in children have not been established. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects, so close monitoring by the doctor is important. Liver or kidney problems: Tell your doctor if you have liver or thyroid problems, as bexarotene can affect these organs and your doctor may need to monitor you more closely or adjust your dose.
